issues.description: HAS_PERCENTAGE regex omits the case-insensitive flag yet KEYWORD walks ignore case — asymmetric, unjustified.
issues.detail: In keyframe-selector-notation, HAS_KEYWORD uses /i but HAS_PERCENTAGE does not. Percentages are digits so case is moot for the literal; however the surrounding selectors may contain mixed-case keywords adjacent to percentages. The author has not stated the invariant that justifies the asymmetry. State it or normalize the flags.

issues.description: The pre-filter regex for selector-pseudo-element-colon-notation is too permissive to actually prune work.
issues.detail: walkRules(/:/) matches any selector containing a colon — including every :hover, :focus, :is(), attribute selectors like [href*=':'], and namespace prefixes. The claimed performance win is small and the precondition 'selector contains a pseudo-element candidate' is not what the regex tests. State the postcondition you intend, then narrow the regex (e.g. /::?[a-z]/i).

issues.description: import-notation 'url' branch silently skips params that contain url() but should still be examined.
issues.detail: The guard `if (primary === 'url' && /url(/i.test(params)) return;` exits when url() is present, on the assumption that url-form is already correct. But @import params may contain url() plus malformed or non-standard-syntax content the downstream walker reports on (e.g. nested constructs, media queries with embedded url tokens). The invariant 'url() present implies no diagnostic needed' is not proved; it is asserted.

issues.description: HAS_NAMED/HAS_NUMERIC regexes constructed without escaping the keyword set — TESTED-NOT-PROVED.
issues.detail: The keyword arrays from referenced constants are joined raw into a RegExp source. If any keyword ever contains a regex metacharacter (hyphen inside a character class context, plus, dot), the regex silently changes meaning. Today the inputs are alphabetic; tomorrow they may not be. A one-line escape or a comment stating the precondition 'all keywords are [a-z]+ only' would suffice.

issues.description: media-feature-range-notation prefilter for 'context' uses /(?:min|max)-/i which matches outside media features.
issues.detail: An @media params string may legitimately contain `min-` or `max-` inside a custom identifier, calc expression, or vendor token without it being a min/max- media feature. The regex is a heuristic, not a specification. It is sound as a pre-filter (false positives only cost work, never correctness), but the comment should state that explicitly so future readers do not tighten it incorrectly.

issues.description: No regression test asserts the early-exit branches preserve diagnostic output — TESTED-NOT-PROVED.
issues.detail: The diff adds fast-path returns across six rules. No test additions appear. The claim 'performance improved without changing semantics' rests on existing tests catching every case the new guards skip. Existing tests are necessary but not sufficient; a targeted test per rule asserting (a) early-exit fires when expected and (b) a value sitting near the regex boundary still reports correctly would convert this from tested-not-proved toward reasoned.

review.summary: The patch is a competent set of pre-filter guards: where the rule's primary option determines that a declaration or selector cannot possibly violate, the walker exits before parsing. The reasoning is sound in spirit but stated nowhere — no precondition, no postcondition, no invariant accompanies any of the six fast paths. Two of the regexes (the bare `/:/` for pseudo-element detection, and the unescaped keyword-joined patterns) are heuristics presented as specifications. The change is TESTED-NOT-PROVED: it relies on the existing test suite catching any case where the guard wrongly excludes work, with no new tests pinning the boundary. Accept with the modest changes above; refuse to call it reasoned until the invariants are written down.
